title: Who Was the Man?
description: A night drive told in the simple past, and the two language points it carries: the many jobs of the word what, sorted by the frame it sits in (What about + noun or -ing for a suggestion, What if for fear and apprehension, What a/an + noun for surprise and appreciation, What do you mean for clarification, What's the ... for ... for information, What + subject + verb + is for insisting, Is this what you ... for satisfaction) and the three grammatical roles behind those frames — interrogative word, exclamation word, and what meaning the thing that; the genitive, with the owner first and the apostrophe placed by the number of owners (the driver's window, the drivers' windows, the children's books, Mr Jones' car), plus the family links it names (daughter-in-law, son-in-law, father-in-law, mother-in-law); why a narration runs on the simple past and how to give the infinitive back for its irregular forms; the words of the road (a journey, a breakdown, the headlights, the rear-view mirror, the steering wheel, to overtake, to brake, to grip, thumping, relieved) and the adjectives that name a narrator's feelings from what her body does; and the three reading tasks of the lesson — true or false with a quotation, putting the events in the order they happen, and inferring only what the words prove
